ov: The largemouth bass, an olive-green freshwater fish with a dark, jagged stripe along each side, native to the eastern and central US, south-eastern Canada and northern Mexico. It is the largest black bass and a prized sport fish, and has been released in many other countries.

why.et: An important food fish around the world, and a hugely popular sport fish in the US.

rg: Native to the eastern and central US, south-eastern Canada and northern Mexico. Introduced widely, including Japan, Namibia, Cuba, Guatemala and the Iberian Peninsula.
df: Young bass eat small fish, water fleas, shrimp and insects; adults eat mostly fish, plus crayfish, frogs, snakes and salamanders. Prey can be half its own length.
fx: It has been blamed for the extinction of the Atitlán grebe, a waterbird of Lake Atitlán in Guatemala.
The male guards the nest until the eggs hatch.
